one_line_contribution: A measurement protocol whose primary endpoint is a 'substitution ratio' S quantifying how much of a procedural-memory bank's paired gain survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is trained on exactly the same episodes, plus the sharper claim that a frozen instruction compiled offline from the whole bank can replace per-instance retrieval at matched injected tokens.
closest_prior_work: Three threats, in descending order. (1) The unverified TERMS-Bench (2605.13909) that the proposal itself says a prior reviewer flagged: if it exists as described, the load-bearing logical move — use a reflective prompt optimizer as the control for a non-prompt intervention — is already published, and the proposal's residual contribution shrinks to 'the same move, applied to memory, with a ratio statistic.' The proposal punts on this rather than resolving it. (2) MemDelta (2606.29914) already owns 'headline agent-memory gains are baseline artifacts,' so the framing paragraph of the abstract is no longer new; the proposal concedes this correctly. (3) EvoClinician (2601.22964) already tables prompt-optimization agents against memory agents, defining memory baselines as 'keep the prompt fixed but add long-term memory' — the three-way comparison exists in the wild, so the novelty rests entirely on the matched-episode constraint, the compiled-static arm, and S itself. Separately, the observation that ExpeL and GEPA implement the same reflect-and-distill principle differing only in storage location is close to folk knowledge in the DSPy/agent-memory community and would not by itself carry a paper.
strongest_objection: S conflates information substitution with generic sub-additivity, and the grid contains no arm that can separate them. Any two interventions that each raise accuracy will fix overlapping instances and show diminishing returns; a high S in cells 5/6 (I1xM0, I1xM1) is exactly what you would observe if GEPA's instruction simply consumed headroom on the easier failure modes, with no transfer of training-episode content at all. The paper's title claim ('memory is just an un-optimized prompt') requires that the optimizer absorbed *the bank's information*, but nothing in the design licenses that inference — I3 controls only for length, not for an accuracy-matched instruction carrying different information. Second, the design's own inference rule sinks its flagship prediction: MDE is stated as ~4 points at n=600 (E1) and ~6 at n=274 (E2), yet Prediction 3 asserts I0xM2 lands 'within 2 points' of I0xM1 and Prediction 7 asserts I0xM1 exceeds I0xM3 by '<3 points.' Both are equivalence claims below the detection floor, and the stated policy ('sub-MDE differences are reported as inconclusive in either direction') means these predictions can be falsified but never confirmed — the 'risky, non-obvious' compile-don't-retrieve result is unwinnable as designed. Prediction 4 has the same defect: the load-bearing positive control predicts a >=5-point I0xM1dup-over-I0xM2dup gap on n=300, where the proposal's own MDE is ~6. Third, the PRECHECK GATE breaks the fairness constraint that makes the study interpretable: a bank that fails is 'enriched (more training episodes, better distillation) until it passes,' but the HELD FIXED section promises that all learned artifacts derive from the same training split, and there is no commitment to re-running GEPA on the enriched split. Enrich-until-pass on a 150-instance dev split is also an unbounded researcher degree of freedom that selects banks whose gain is inflated by dev-set noise, and the winner's-curse regression on the 600-instance test split shrinks S's denominator — precisely the instability the gate was introduced to prevent. Fourth, the track's own starting position reports memory fixing zero items and breaking six to seven under paired evaluation; the entire 7-cell grid is gated on reproducing a >=10-point memory gain that in-house evidence suggests may be unreachable, in which case the primary endpoint is never computed in either environment.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Add an information-disjoint optimizer arm and make it a required cell, not an ablation: run GEPA on training episodes disjoint from those used to build the bank (or on a related-but-different task pool), select the variant whose I1'xM0 accuracy matches I1xM0, and report S computed against it. If S is equally high there, the effect is headroom, not substitution, and the paper's thesis is dead; if S is materially lower, the substitution claim is earned. (2) Restate Predictions 3 and 7 as formal non-inferiority tests with a margin at or above the MDE, or raise resolution (per-instance F1 with a continuous paired test rather than binary EM, more decoding seeds, larger E1 pool) until a 2-point equivalence is actually detectable; otherwise drop the '2 points' number and pre-commit to reporting a CI. (3) Pre-register the bank-construction procedure with a hard iteration cap, apply the gate on a split used for nothing else, and require that if the bank is enriched with additional training episodes then GEPA is re-run on the identical enriched split — otherwise the matched-information premise is void. (4) Restore one environment where task structure does not recur across train and test (the cut WebShop, or a compositional held-out split of MuSiQue), since both retained environments were selected for maximal compilability and the compilation prediction is currently only tested where it is most likely to succeed. (5) Replace or supplement B-dup with a non-synthetic non-compilable control; near-duplicate leakage is instance-specific episodic value, which the proposal explicitly scopes out, so passing it does not establish sensitivity to diffuse, genuinely procedural non-substitutable value — which is the null the paper wants to interpret. (6) Resolve the TERMS-Bench question before submission; an unresolved closest structural precedent is not a residual risk, it is the novelty question.
missing_baseline: The accuracy-matched, information-disjoint instruction arm (call it I1'xM1: an optimized instruction that improves over I0 by the same margin as I1 but was optimized on episodes the bank never saw). Without it, S cannot distinguish substitution from ordinary sub-additivity of two overlapping interventions, and this is the single cell a reviewer will demand. A close second: the cut I2 (optimize with memory in context). The proposal dismisses it as 'co-adaptation, not substitution,' but the research track's actual open question is the division of labour between the two containers, and a paper that recommends 'compile, don't retrieve' without ever measuring the jointly-optimized configuration cannot say whether the recommendation beats what practitioners would actually deploy. Minor but concrete: the C arm is specified as 'token-matched per instance' while being a single frozen static block, which is not well defined — a frozen instruction can only match the mean retrieval length, so long-retrieval instances are systematically under-matched in a way that biases Prediction 3 toward the null it wants.
preprint_collision: Unusually honest and unusually incomplete, and on balance a weakness. Credit where due: the check retracts five citations (ActMem 2603.00026, MAS-PromptBench 2606.23664, TERMS-Bench 2605.13909, MemAPO 2603.21520, and 2602.11243) as unverifiable and refuses to lean on them, and it correctly concedes that MemDelta (2606.29914) now owns the general 'memory baselines are confounded' thesis. But a search process that demonstrably produced five unverifiable references in the prior draft gives me no basis to trust the surviving ones — MemDelta, EvoClinician (2601.22964), 2603.18272, 2603.02473 and 2605.21768 are all load-bearing for the novelty argument and all arrive with the same provenance; I cannot verify any of them from the submission. More seriously, the single work identified as the closest structural precedent — TERMS-Bench, described as a GEPA-based substitution test for a non-prompt intervention — is left unresolved with a conditional ('if that work exists as described, I would cite it as such'). That is exactly the collision that would decide novelty, and deferring it is not a resolution. Finally, the proposal states it could not sweep OpenReview 2026 submissions; for an ICLR 2027 submission whose nearest competitor would be a 'memory + prompt optimizer' ablation table, that venue is the most likely place for the scoop, and the omission is the one gap the authors could have closed cheaply. Net: no confirmed collision on the specific claim, but novelty is asserted rather than established.
